qualities.label: Calm
qualities.description: Explore the purported calm quality and the limits of ingredient research on relaxation-related experiences. No finished-spray effect is established.

qualities.label: Focus
qualities.description: Explore the purported focus quality through short-term aroma, attention and memory research. Findings can be mixed and do not establish everyday performance benefits.

qualities.label: Sleep / wind-down
qualities.description: Explore the purported sleep / wind-down quality. Ingredient sleep studies do not establish that this cosmetic spray improves sleep or treats a sleep condition.

qualities.label: Uplifting
qualities.description: Explore the purported uplifting quality through limited studies of subjective contentment and mood. These are not claims of a lasting mood benefit from the spray.

record.name: Lemon
record.description: Cold-pressed from lemon peel. Dominated by limonene, which gives it the sharp citrus character used across cleaning, fragrance, and flavor work.

precautions.legacySafety: Phototoxic on skin in sunlight; avoid undiluted topical use.

qualityMappings.summary: Research relevant to the purported calm quality: a small randomized study reported lower test-anxiety scores after a brief exposure to lemon essential-oil aroma than in its control group.
qualityMappings.limitations: 46 nursing students and one acute test setting. This is whole lemon oil, not isolated limonene; the result does not establish treatment of anxiety or lasting relaxation. No evidence of the effectiveness or safety of this finished spray or a custom combination is established by this study.

blend.sensitizationNotes: No verified sensitization assessment yet for this oil in the proposed leave-on spray. Legacy profile notes are unaudited and do not establish formulation safety.
blend.legacySafetyNotes: Phototoxic on skin in sunlight; avoid undiluted topical use.
researchGaps: Earlier citrus-fragrance research is not treated as lemon-only evidence for an uplifting quality.
No verified focus, sleep or uplifting mapping for this oil is provided in the starter catalog.

record.name: Lavender
record.description: Steam-distilled flowering tops with a floral, herbal aroma. Linalool and linalyl acetate are prominent in many analyzed samples.

constituents.basis: ISO 11024 specification cited in GC-MS study

precautions.legacySafety: Generally well tolerated; patch test for sensitive skin.

qualityMappings.summary: Research relevant to the purported calm quality: a trial of lavender aromatherapy massage reported lower salivary cortisol immediately after treatment than usual care.
qualityMappings.limitations: Whole lavender oil was used with massage in 52 pregnant participants. There was no massage-only comparison, so the contribution of the oil cannot be separated from massage. Cortisol is not a direct measure of feeling calm. This does not establish safety during pregnancy. No evidence of the effectiveness or safety of this finished spray or a custom combination is established by this study.

qualityMappings.summary: Counterevidence for the purported calm quality: a randomized trial of a lavender, bergamot and cedarwood aroma mixture did not show benefit; the carrier-only group had lower anxiety scores than the fragrant groups at treatment completion.
qualityMappings.limitations: This was a multi-oil intervention in 313 radiotherapy patients. Its findings cannot be assigned to lavender alone or generalized to everyday cosmetic use. No evidence of the effectiveness or safety of this finished spray or a custom combination is established by this study.

qualityMappings.summary: Research relevant to the purported sleep / wind-down quality: a review combining 11 randomized trials reported better adult sleep-quality scores with lavender essential-oil interventions overall.
qualityMappings.limitations: Review of whole-oil interventions, not isolated linalool. Study quality, routes, concentrations and duration varied; some subgroup results were not significant. This does not establish treatment of insomnia or an effective spray formulation. No evidence of the effectiveness or safety of this finished spray or a custom combination is established by this study.

blend.sensitizationNotes: No verified sensitization assessment yet for this oil in the proposed leave-on spray. Legacy profile notes are unaudited and do not establish formulation safety.
blend.legacySafetyNotes: Generally well tolerated; patch test for sensitive skin.
researchGaps: No verified finished-product study or tested custom-blend ratio is provided in this catalog.
Standardized oral lavender preparations and isolated-compound findings are not used as evidence that this topical spray has the same effects.

record.name: Peppermint
record.description: Steam-distilled from leaves. Menthol activates cold receptors, which is why it reads as cooling on skin and airways.

precautions.legacySafety: Keep away from young children; can irritate eyes and mucous membranes.

qualityMappings.summary: Research relevant to the purported focus quality: peppermint whole-oil aroma was associated with better memory measures and higher self-rated alertness in a laboratory study.
qualityMappings.limitations: Single-session aroma exposure in healthy volunteers. This is whole-oil evidence, not a trial of isolated menthol, and does not establish improved everyday work or study performance. No evidence of the effectiveness or safety of this finished spray or a custom combination is established by this study.

record.name: Rosemary

precautions.legacySafety: Avoid in pregnancy and with epilepsy; may raise blood pressure.

qualityMappings.summary: Research relevant to the purported focus quality: rosemary whole-oil aroma improved some memory-quality measures and relative alertness in a laboratory study, but also slowed memory speed.
qualityMappings.limitations: Mixed outcomes after a single brief exposure in healthy adults. Better results on some tasks do not establish general cognitive enhancement. No evidence of the effectiveness or safety of this finished spray or a custom combination is established by this study.

qualityMappings.summary: Research relevant to the purported focus quality: after rosemary whole-oil aroma exposure, blood 1,8-cineole levels correlated with performance on some cognitive tasks.
qualityMappings.limitations: Small correlational study of 20 volunteers. The exposure was whole rosemary oil; measuring one constituent does not establish that isolated 1,8-cineole caused the results, or that other oils containing it have the same effect. No evidence of the effectiveness or safety of this finished spray or a custom combination is established by this study.

qualityMappings.summary: Research relevant to the purported uplifting quality: the rosemary-aroma group reported greater contentment than the no-aroma control group after cognitive testing.
qualityMappings.limitations: Subjective mood finding from one short laboratory exposure in healthy adults, alongside mixed cognitive outcomes. This is not evidence for treatment of a mood condition or a lasting change in mood. No evidence of the effectiveness or safety of this finished spray or a custom combination is established by this study.

blend.legacySafetyNotes: Avoid in pregnancy and with epilepsy; may raise blood pressure.
researchGaps: Studies of swallowed rosemary leaf or powder are not treated as evidence for rosemary essential oil in a spray.

qualityMappings.summary: Research relevant to the purported calm quality: students using bergamot whole-oil aroma stones reported lower state-anxiety scores before examinations than students using water stones.

studies.authors: Pinto L, Cervellieri S, Netti T, Lippolis V, Baruzzi F.
studies.finding: Oregano oil vapor reduced culturable bacteria on steel, polypropylene and glass coupons. Most tested combinations had no detectable viable cells; one Staphylococcus/glass combination retained survivors.

studies.title: Antimicrobial and hand hygiene effects of Tea Tree Essential Oil disinfectant: A randomised control trial
studies.authors: Youn BH, Kim YS, Yoo S, Hur MH.
studies.finding: A randomized trial in 112 adults compared a 10% tea-tree formulation, alcohol, benzalkonium chloride and no treatment. Post-treatment bacterial counts differed among groups; the abstract does not establish equivalence or superiority to alcohol.
studies.limitations: Specific 10% formulation with solubilizer and glycerin. Short-term hand measurements, not infection rates, arbitrary dilution advice or surface-disinfection evidence.

chemicalGroups.label: Aldehydes
chemicalGroups.description: A fragrant functional group found across chemical families. Citral gives lemongrass its lemony character; cinnamaldehyde is associated with cinnamon.
chemicalGroups.details: An aldehyde contains a terminal carbonyl group (-CHO). Citral is a mixture of geranial and neral. Citral and citronellal remain monoterpenoids; cinnamaldehyde remains a phenylpropanoid.

chemicalGroups.label: Esters
chemicalGroups.description: Many volatile esters contribute floral or fruity notes. Linalyl acetate is an example associated with lavender and bergamot.
chemicalGroups.details: An ester functional group can overlap with a primary chemical family. Linalyl acetate is both a monoterpenoid and an acetate ester. Not all esters are volatile or fragrant.

chemicalGroups.label: Thiols
chemicalGroups.description: Some sulfur-containing volatiles affect aroma at trace levels. Examples have been reported in grapefruit oil and in cannabis flower or extract research.
chemicalGroups.details: Thiols contain a sulfur-hydrogen (-SH) group. Other volatile sulfur compounds include sulfides and thioesters, so not every sulfur volatile is a thiol.

chemicalGroups.label: Flavonoids
chemicalGroups.description: Typically nonvolatile plant polyphenols. They belong to broader plant chemistry and are not generally aroma molecules or dominant constituents of steam-distilled oils.
chemicalGroups.details: Cannflavins illustrate plant-material chemistry. Nobiletin is documented in nonvolatile fractions of some cold-pressed citrus oils. These findings stay separate from volatile fingerprints. LC/HPLC methods are commonly used for flavonoids.

audit.scope: Library-first mapping with targeted primary-source verification; not an exhaustive literature review.
audit.researchMatchMeaning: Verified matching of the named oil to the exact research topic, including negative, null, mixed and mechanistic findings. It does not assert positive clinical benefit, safe dosing, finished-product efficacy or formulation compatibility.
audit.outcomeMeaning: Verification, material, model and outcome are independent facets. Unverified means unknown, never a negative result.

independentReview.scope: All existing publication identities checked and available abstracts screened; this is not full-text verification of every oil-study edge, quantitative composition value or safety threshold. Prior endpoint verification remains independent.
